key_insight: A steady component flux can induce a pinned condensed annulus in an otherwise stable binary mixture through an effective logarithmic field.
engineering_relevance: Semipermeable boundary transport could control where condensation or cavitation occurs in radial systems without changing the critical temperature.
method: Model binary-mixture transport in a two-dimensional annulus using Model B dynamics.
Map steady transport to an equilibrium profile in a self-consistent logarithmic field.
Derive condensation thresholds and interfacial-tension effects, then test with numerical solutions.
evidence_signal: Numerical solutions confirm the analytical predictions and reveal hysteresis bounded by two saddle-node bifurcations.
watch_item: The predictions rely on radial geometry and Model B dynamics; applicability to systems with hydrodynamic flow or turbulence remains unestablished.
paper_title: Flux-induced condensation in a radial geometry
